get.description: Returns List of Assets by given Company and Project

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the company.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the project.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search query. Searches across: asset_id (asset_code), asset_name, description, created_by (user name), modified_by (user name), asset_type (name), asset_status (name), trade (name), and custom field values.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: The view type

parameters.name: include_profile_image
parameters.description: Include profile image URLs in response. Profile image URLs are included in all views when this parameter is true.

parameters.name: include_bim_info
parameters.description: Include BIM scene and object information in response. BIM info is included when this parameter is true.

parameters.name: wrap_custom_fields
parameters.description: When true, wraps each custom field value as {"value": ...} and renames "name" to "label" inside LOV objects.

parameters.name: can_link_with
parameters.description: When provided with normal or extended view, each asset includes a 'linkable' boolean indicating whether it can be linked with the specified item type. Supported values: PublicDomainApi::BimModelContext.

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Filter by asset IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'id1,id2,id3').

parameters.name: filters[asset_type_id]
parameters.description: Filter by asset type IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'typeId1,typeId2').

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description: Created at filter (date range format: YYYY-MM-DD...YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ...YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)

parameters.name: filters[modified_at]
parameters.description: Updated at filter (date range format: YYYY-MM-DD...YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ...YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)

parameters.name: filters[asset_status_id]
parameters.description: Filter by asset status IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'statusId1,statusId2').

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Filter by location IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'locId1,locId2').

parameters.name: filters[trade_id]
parameters.description: Filter by trade IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'tradeId1,tradeId2').

parameters.name: filters[scene_id]
parameters.description: Filter by BIM scene IDs. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'sceneId1,sceneId2').

parameters.name: filters[asset_code]
parameters.description: Filter by asset IDs (asset_code in API, also referred as asset_id). Case-insensitive. Accepts a single ID or multiple comma-separated IDs (e.g., 'ASSET-001,ASSET-002').

parameters.name: filters[custom_field_id]
parameters.description: Filter by custom field values. Supported only for single select, multi-select, and datetime fields. Can be used multiple times for different custom fields. Supports single values (e.g., 'filters[custom_field_123]=id1'), comma-separated values for multi-select (e.g., 'filters[custom_field_456]=id1,id2'), Datetime range with '...' separator: 'filters[custom_field_789]=2024-01-01...2024-12-31' or 'filters[custom_field_789]=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z...2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sorting criteria in minus-based order format. Default sort order is ascending. Multiple sort criteria can be provided in CSV format, for example: sort=asset_name,-modified_at.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page index (1..N)

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The size of the page to be returned

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

post.summary: Link Sub-Assets to a Parent Asset
post.description: Links one or more existing assets as sub-assets of the parent asset identified by asset_id within the given project. All-or-nothing: any hierarchy rule violation rejects the whole call with HTTP 422. When the parent's ancestor chain is not in the children's project and cascadeAncestors is false (default), the call is rejected with HTTP 409; retry with cascadeAncestors=true to pull the ancestors into the project.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the company.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the project.

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the parent asset

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

schema.description: Request body for linking multiple existing assets as sub-assets of a parent asset. The parent is identified by the path variable; this DTO carries the children to link.

asset_ids.description: Asset ids to link as sub-assets of the parent asset. Must contain at least one id and no more than 500 ids.

items.description: Asset ids to link as sub-assets of the parent asset. Must contain at least one id and no more than 500 ids.

cascade_ancestors.description: If true, transparently pull the parent's ancestor chain into the children's project when the chain is not already there. If false (default), the request returns 409 listing the ancestors that need pulling in so the UI can prompt for confirmation.

schema.description: Response for the Link Sub-Assets operation

data.description: Successful response for the Link-Sub-Assets endpoint. Returned only when every selected asset was linked; rule violations surface as 422 instead.

linked_count.description: Number of assets linked as sub-assets in this request.

linked_asset_ids.description: Asset ids that were linked as sub-assets of the parent.

items.description: Asset ids that were linked as sub-assets of the parent.

message.description: Human-readable summary, e.g. "12 assets linked as sub-assets of PUMP-001".

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("localhost:8080")

headers = {
    'Procore-Company-Id': "SOME_INTEGER_VALUE",
    'Accept-Language': "SOME_STRING_VALUE"
    }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.0/companies/1234/projects/1234/assets/by_code/%7Basset_code%7D?wrap_custom_fields=SOME_BOOLEAN_VALUE", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
